quotes.text: My Morning Jacket has never been a band afraid to take risks, finding success by going their own eccentric way.
Circuital is the band's sixth studio album since their inception in 1998, and while it's bizarre at times and humorous at others, it is uniquely My Morning Jacket, and that's a fine thing.
In Circuital, the 13-year-old band led by the 33-year-old James certainly went for it, proving that they are still an incredibly fresh voice in an increasingly stale music world.
This bizarre beginning illustrates the band's narcissistic motto: channeling the band's visceral, inner voice won't get it radio airplay.
This song is emblematic of the hodge-podge of sounds that make this album so impressive.
Known for an ability to procure many different styles of sound, My Morning Jacket have swept the country with unique sound, accumulating to 26 years of music now behind them.

This upbeat and funky energy evolves in a more classic dad rock feel for "Everyday Magic" with the building of My Morning Jacket's signature oddities and effects cycling under the easy chorus and lyrics.
A cinematic build climaxes with piercing electric guitar lines, bringing the true rock back in the My Morning Jacket sound.
Touching into a psychedelic-rock sound the melodies ebb and flow like hot sun on a desert summer day.

There is no question that this band are feeling the pressure of time steady passing, though the ability to channel it all into sound will keep their energy immortal. It seems no matter how many albums My Morning Jacket put out, the ending of a project will always hold a somber note.
My Morning Jacket likes to hide some of its best music behind unassuming titles.
Nearing their third decade as a band, My Morning Jacket's veterancy shines on "is." They continue to improve on their ability to write melodic and focused psychedelic rock songs.

For "is," My Morning Jacket handed the producer duties over to Brendan O'Brien, who has worked with Phish, Bruce Springsteen and Pearl Jam — a rarity for a band that prefers to self-produce and has for nearly a decade.
O'Brien doesn't mess with the sound that My Morning Jacket fans love and expect. Instead, he seems to have focused the band in a way that allows them to deliver a unified, 10-song collection.
